auditor_jane: Hi team — during next-week fieldwork the auditor asked for consolidated evidence covering:
- RBAC changes (from 2024-09-01 to present)
- KMS key rotation proof and key custody mapping
- Audit/log retention proof (S3/SIEM exports)
- One example vuln triage with incident linkage
Can you point to presigned artifacts or a reproducible extraction plan? Thanks :eyes:

sec_engineer_lee: Thanks @auditor_jane. I'll assemble a bundle and drop links. Quick callouts now:
- RBAC: exported rolebindings + policy change log snapshots
  e.g. `kubectl get rolebinding --all-namespaces -o yaml > /tmp/rb_bindings-2026-03-21.yaml`
- KMS: rotation manifest and rotation event log (KMS key id + rotation timestamps)
- Audit logs: S3 paths + SIEM query examples for correlation
I can generate a signed manifest + sha256 checksums. ETA EOD PST.

infra_ops_maya: Adding SIEM examples for reproducible queries (Splunk/Kusto style):
- Splunk: `index=redwood_audit action=\"role_change\" earliest=\"09/01/2024:00:00:00\" | table _time user target_field change`
- Kusto: `RedwoodAudit | where Action == \"RoleChanged\" and TimeGenerated >= datetime(2024-09-01)`
Also note: we archive logs to s3://redwood-compliance/audit-archives/ with lifecycle policy 7y.

eng_sre_noah: For incident linkage, see INC-2024-1123 (pagerduty link in ticket). Summary: privilege escalation vuln CVE-2024-9999 detected -> triggered alert -> infra playbook executed -> role binding reverted. Timeline export placed at: /evidence/incidents/INC-2024-1123/timeline.json

compliance_paul: Please ensure the bundle includes:
- chain-of-custody metadata (who exported, when)
- signed manifest (PGP sig) and sha256 sums
- mapping doc: control ID -> evidence file (SOC2 CC6.1 / ISO 27001 A.9 mappings)
We need the control mapping table in simple CSV.

sec_engineer_lee: Got it. Uploaded staged bundle and artifacts (short refs):
- RBAC exports: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/2026-03/rbac-exports-20260321.tar.gz
- KMS rotation: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/2026-03/kms-rotation-manifest-20260321.json
- Incident package: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/2026-03/inc-2024-1123-package.zip
- Control map CSV: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/2026-03/control-mapping-soc2-iso.csv
Files hashed and signed: `checksums-1715123456.json` + `manifest-1715123456.sig`
Presigned download (1h): https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-compliance/evidence/1715123456-bundle.zip?X-Amz-Expires=3600
Password for zip sent to auditors via secure channel. @compliance_paul please confirm this flow. :lock:

compliance_paul: Confirmed the flow. Need the CSV mapping to include exact control IDs and evidence file names. Also confirm KMS key rotation log includes the key ARN and the principal who initiated rotation (for custody).

sec_engineer_lee: Confirmed — rotation log contains `KeyId`, `RotationDate`, `InitiatingPrincipal`. Example snippet we included: 
```
{
  \"KeyId\": \"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345\",
  \"RotationDate\": \"2025-11-02T03:12:45Z\",
  \"InitiatingPrincipal\": \"iam::123456789012:role/keystore-admin\"
}
```
Checksums file: `sha256sum rbac-exports-20260321.tar.gz`

oncall_bot: evidence-bundler: Bundle 1715123456 created by sec_engineer_lee, size=42MB, files=9, expires=7 days, manifest=checksums-1715123456.json :package:

auditor_jane: Thanks — can you also provide one short walkthrough (3–5 steps) auditors can run to validate the RBAC export contains the expected role change? They like deterministic steps.

sec_engineer_lee: Yep. Walkthrough (audit runner):
1) Download `rbac-exports-20260321.tar.gz` (presigned link above).
2) `tar xzf rbac-exports-20260321.tar.gz`
3) `grep -A2 \"changedBy: alice@example.com\" */*.yaml` (replace principal)
4) Verify timestamp and diff against baseline `git diff --no-index baseline/ current/`
5) Check `checksums-1715123456.json` signature with our PGP key (pubkey on compliance repo)

infra_ops_maya: If auditors want live SIEM evidence we can run the Splunk query and export raw events to CSV; note that exports will also be placed under the same S3 evidence prefix.

compliance_paul: All reasonable. Once @auditor_jane confirms, I'll mark the bundle as official deliverable and stamp with the chain-of-custody entry.

auditor_jane: Looks good. I will validate the bundle this afternoon and follow up if anything missing. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :tada:
